findings.explanation: The flagged line executes a SQL query built with an f-string that interpolates `sort_by`. However, `sort_by` is taken from `request.args.get('sort_by', 'created_at')` and is strictly validated against the hard-coded allowlist `ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS = {'created_at', 'total', 'status', 'id'}`; any value not in the set returns a 400 error before the query is built. This is exactly the mitigation the project's security policy prescribes for dynamic identifiers (sort keys). No user-controlled value can reach the query outside the four whitelisted column names, so this is a false positive.

evidence.content: Dynamic identifiers (table or column names, sort keys) MUST be validated against a hard-coded allowlist before being placed in a query.

findings.explanation: The new GET /orders/sorted endpoint is a list-all-orders operation (it returns every order row, not scoped to the requester). Per security-policy.md §3, 'Managers and admins may list all orders (GET /orders/all)', and api-spec.md documents the analogous list-all endpoint '/orders/all | GET | manager, admin'. The changed code enforces this with @require_role("manager") (app/routes/orders.py, added lines), which is the exact decorator the policy mandates (security-policy.md §1: 'Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in app/auth.py'). app/auth.py:69-85 confirms require_role authenticates the bearer token and enforces ROLE_RANK (user<manager<admin), so only manager/admin pass. This matches the access level of the existing /orders/all endpoint (app/routes/orders.py:50-51, also @require_role("manager")). The endpoint is not a per-object fetch, so the is_owner_or_admin ownership check is not required. Note: the SQL uses an f-string with a request-derived sort key, but it is validated against the hard-coded ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS allowlist, satisfying security-policy.md §5's dynamic-identifier rule; that is a SQL-injection concern outside this authorization review.

evidence.content: Managers and admins may list all orders (`GET /orders/all`).
Endpoints MUST use the decorators provided in `app/auth.py` (`@require_auth`, `@require_role`, `@require_api_key_scope`).
